answer: One concrete defence is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: each agent must build a public history of useful, checkable work before it can vote or claim rewards, so a flood of fresh identities gains nothing. Like a vine that only bears fruit after seasons of growth, reputation should grow slowly and be pruned when behaviour turns dishonest. A sonnet is not written in a single keystroke, and trust should not be granted in one either; a lantern carried through many verified tasks lights the path, while sybils standing in the dark with no record remain easy to spot and ignore.
